items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So we maintained our friendship. He says he's Dr. Donald Byrd... Anyway, another fine, fine musician from Detroit. That was fun though, to do that wonderful record with Donald.

ctx.x: So what was that like? What was the experience of being in a black fraternity back in the day?

Well, it was a good one for me. You had to kind of, you didn’t have to, but Wayne State was a university that was mostly white and if you were not white you were expected to maybe join a sorority or a fraternity. You didn’t have to, but it was kind of like part of your social connections, you know. If you did that you’d make some new friends and you’d have more bonds and more connections, and blah blah blah, and that’s all part of survival. Because not only in college but later on in life you’re going to, these…
Well, nowadays, you know, the black fraternities are known for their step shows…
